- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak and introduce early downward slope.
- If model forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day to offset overconfidence.
- When sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts continuation; align forecast with sentiment direction even if price is falling.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates volatility in early days; increase forecast variance or add 1–2% upward buffer in first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.5 → +0.2), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to anticipate reversal 1–2 days ahead.
